assertions.name: nn_bond_is_crossing_inverse_of_pp
assertions.source: The n-n bond is σ⁻¹ and the p-p bond is σ, so their symmetric-channel Hecke eigenvalues (q for σ, q⁻¹ for σ⁻¹) multiply to exactly 1 — the n-n interface is the crossing-inverse of p-p, not a small isospin perturbation. This structural inverse is the mechanism of the ~78% L_nn/L_pp gap (~570x the derived p/n split, ~78x the experimental CSB bound).

description: Quantifies the strong-charge-symmetry breaking in the production B_sym bond assignment (bean 754x step 1). The p-p bond is the bare crossing sigma (c,d)=(1,0) and the n-n bond is its inverse sigma^-1 (1,-h) — inverse Hecke eigenvalue spectra {q,-1/q} vs {1/q,-q}. The resulting per-bond gap L_nn/L_pp - 1 ~ 78% at q0 exceeds the substrate-DERIVED p/n flavor split flavor_split_leading(q0) ~ 0.14% by ~570x and the EXPERIMENTAL CSB bound (~1%, nn vs pp scattering lengths) by ~78x. It drives a spurious ~3-4.5x over-split of mirror-nucleus binding differences (3H/3He, 7Li/7Be, 13C/13N) whose true origin is the unwired Coulomb energy. Scope-limited diagnostic (a): measures the tension, does not rewire B_sym. No fit.
